hypotheses.root_cause: Poor heatsink/TIM contact left a large die-to-ambient thermal resistance, so even after the DVFS step-down the junction temperature jumped past the 105 °C trip point.
hypotheses.rationale: The only evidence marker in the run is the heatsink tell-tale: 'Sensor-to-ambient delta high | delta_c=71' at 291 ms, logged right after 'Temperature high' (95 °C). The full log has no 'Power burst detected' or 'p_w=' lines, which rules against RC_WORKLOAD_BURST, even though the two closest past incidents (000015 and 000020) were bursts and both had a PMU burst line. It also has no 'Fan speed below profile' line, which rules against RC_FAN_PROFILE_BAD. The DVFS step-down at 461 ms (800 to 600 MHz) held the sensors at 93–97 °C, but cooling could not hold, and t_c=115 was reached at 831 ms. That points to a cooling shortfall rather than extra power. Two things lower my confidence: the logged ambient_c=95 together with delta_c=71 is not physically consistent, so the fields may be mislabelled; and there was a sudden jump from 96 °C at 731 ms to 115 °C at 831 ms with no PMU INFO checked in that gap.
recommended_actions: Re-seat the heatsink and replace the TIM, then rerun the same workload and compare the die-to-ambient delta (should drop well below 71 C)
Measure heatsink mounting pressure and flatness against the thermal spec
Verify ambient/delta sensor field mapping in the THERMAL logger (ambient_c=95 looks mislabelled) and check PMU INFO telemetry 731-831 ms to exclude an unlogged power step
Cross-check fan tach readings during the run to confirm the fan met its profile

Temperature climbed past the DVFS policy and crossed the 105C trip point before throttling could recover it, triggering an emergency shutdown — a cooling-solution or fan-profile shortfall under sustained workload.

- RC_HEATSINK_POOR: Poor heatsink/TIM contact — large die-to-ambient delta
    tell-tales: sensor-to-ambient delta high, delta_c
    actions: Re-seat the heatsink and replace the TIM; Measure mounting pressure against the thermal spec
- RC_FAN_PROFILE_BAD: Fan speed stays below the profile target as temperature rises
    tell-tales: fan speed below profile, target_rpm
    actions: Fix the fan curve / PWM mapping in the thermal policy; Verify tachometer feedback and fan power
- RC_WORKLOAD_BURST: A sustained power burst outruns the cooling headroom
    tell-tales: power burst detected, p_w=
    actions: Cap the burst power or lengthen the DVFS step-down reaction; Add thermal headroom to the test's power envelope
